Project Objective:
To test the hypothesis that ETS exposure has an adverse effect on pregnancy
outcome.
Project Summary:
Prospective study using nested study design. Women enrolled within 12 weeks of
last menstrual period are invited to join an intensively monitored group with
four exposure assessments during pregnancy. All other study participants are
randomized either to biochemical monitoring which involves three exposure
assessments, or telephone monitoring which involves a single assessment.
Intensive Monitoring: Eligibility requirements were changed in Oct 1989.
Before that date a woman had to have entered study within 12 weeks of her Tast
menstrual period to be eligible. Since then, in addition, a woman must have
reported direct and/or passive smoke exposure during her pregnancy. (The goal
is to have 300 women in this group with completed pregnancies and ali exposure
monitoring completed.) Monitoring includes: Wearing a personal monitor
(passive nicotine monitor) 4 times during pregnancy (for 7 days each time). At
the end of each 7 day period the women are asked to provide a urine sample and
to answer a brief questionnaire. At one of the 4 periods they are also asked
to place an air monitor (passive nicotine monitor) in their home and workplace
(if applicable).
